newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel steady to slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel steady to slightly lower.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices were steady to a tad lower on Thursday despite news of lower middle-distillate inventory in Singapore, traders said.
Middle-distillate stocks fell a hefty 1.078 million barrels to 7.786 million barrels which traders said indicated the effect of cut in refinery runs since the past one month.
But they noted that slow regional demand was dampening sentiment, coupled with persistent talk that several traders were considering to bring in northwest European cargoes to this region.

One trader were said to have sold about 500,000 barrels of gas oil swaps to lock in the East-West spread which traders said could be in anticipation of the arbitrage cargoes. Another US trader were said to be buying as well as selling gas oil swaps.
March swaps was last traded at $25.69 a barrel down from an earlier trade of $25.80.
On the physical market, a Singapore trader sold 150,000 barrels of gas oil to a Swiss trader at $25.45 a barrel for March 18-22 lifting fob. This was higher than the previous deal of $25.30.
Traders said China recently bought from a major 30,000-35,000 tonnes of gas oil at $202 a a tonne, cost-and-freight southern China. Sellers were now indicating at $204-$205 c&f.
The major also sold 20,000 tonnes of gas oil at $1.10 a barrel above Singapore spot quotes c&f Hong Kong.
Taiwan sold two gas oil cargoes at around $25.60 a barrel in its tender for March 1-12 lifting fob, in line with current market level.

Traders said India was expected to buy about 700,000 tonnes of gas oil in its tender for April delivery. They described the volume as having a "neutral" effect on the market. The tender closed on Thursday and would be awarded late on Friday.
India has also issued a tender to buy April-arrival kerosene which closes on March 6.

Traders said a jet fuel cargo was sold for delivery to Taiwan at a premium of $1.50-$1.55 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, c&f. Traders said this would be in line with current fob Singapore premiums of 40 cents per barrel.
Other than this deal, the jet fuel market has been dormant recently as north Asia came out of its cold season.
